newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans ends up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans ends up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Thursday on speculative buying by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,200 yuan ($386) per tonne, rising 11 yuan. It opened at a low of 3,180 yuan per tonne.
November fell four yuan to 3,164, the January 1998 contract rose six to 3,158 and March put on two to 3,150 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 24,100 tonnes from 23,700 tonnes.
Soybeans opened little changed but rose slightly for the rest of the session, traders said.
"Speculative buying by retail investors dominated today's trading with many institutions continuing to stay on the sidelines," one trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to continue moving in a narrow range in the next few days.
